items.title: Voter turnout way up during advance polling in Mississauga
items.summary: More than 44,000 people in Mississauga cast their ballots early at advance voting stations over the past week in the leadup to the 2026 municipal election, the city says. The 44,049 advance votes cast during the six days of early voting between Oct. 6-11 set a new mark for the city and represents a 57 per cent increase compared to advance voting in the 2022 municipal election, the City of Mississauga said on Tuesday. Voters in Canada’s seventh-largest city cast 28,052 early ballots four years ago and 19,188 in the weeks prior to the 2018 municipal election, according to numbers provided by the City of Mississauga. During the 2024 mayoral byelection in Mississauga, 24,731 people went to the polls early. The number of 2026 early ballots cast by day, the city noted, were as follows: “The strong participation during advance voting is encouraging,” Diana Rusnov, City of Mississauga clerk and director of legislative services, said. ” With advance voting over, the next and final chance for eligible residents to cast their ballots is election day, Oct. 26. m. m. On election day, residents can vote at any voting location within their ward. They’ll be casting ballots for mayor of Mississauga (14 candidates), city councillors (11 wards) and school board trustees.

items.title: Police Arrest Suspect After Midday Stabbing Near Hurontario and Dundas in Mississauga
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say a male suspect has been arrested in connection with a stabbing that happened near Hurontario Street and Dundas Street early Tuesday afternoon. According to police, the victim, described only as a male, was rushed to hospital with serious injuries and is now in stable condition. Insauga.com reports a large police presence remained on the scene after the attack as investigators and other officers spoke with people and canvassed the area. The outlet says motorists and others were urged to avoid the area while the stabbing was investigated as an isolated incident. Insauga.com notes the incident came nearly five months after a man was stabbed to death in an unrelated attack in the same area of the city.

items.title: OPP Charge Mississauga Man After Dark Web Drug Shipments Yield 600 Grams of Fentanyl
items.summary: According to the OPP, an investigation into drugs purchased on a dark web marketplace and shipped through the mail has led to charges against a Mississauga man. The OPP says the Caledon Community Street Crime Unit and the Covert Internet Intelligence Unit began investigating suspected drug shipments moving through the mail earlier in the summer. Officers say they arrested a suspect on Aug. 25 at a Canada Post location in Mississauga and seized two packages containing various drugs bound for addresses across Canada. The arrest led to raids of several residences and vehicles across the Greater Toronto Area, where the OPP says officers seized about 600 grams of suspected fentanyl, about 35 grams of suspected cocaine, $40,000 in cash, drug trafficking paraphernalia and numerous electronic devices. The OPP says Jermoll Bain, 33, of Mississauga, faces 16 counts of failing to comply with a release order, nine counts of possessing proceeds of crime over $5,000, and trafficking-related charges, while Jermaine Willis, 34, of North York, has been charged with possessing proceeds of crime over $5,000. Bain was due in a Brampton court Tuesday, and Willis is scheduled to appear Oct. 29, according to the OPP.

items.title: No Incumbent as Six Candidates Vie for Peel School Board Seat in Mississauga Wards 1 and 7
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports six candidates are competing for the Peel District School Board trustee seat covering Mississauga Wards 1 and 7 in the Oct. 26 election. According to the outlet, there is no incumbent in the race because sitting trustee Leeann Cole is instead running for the city's Ward 2 council seat. The outlet says Metroland sent a questionnaire to everyone on the ballot to help voters compare the candidates. Candidate Charles Corey told Metroland he serves as co-chair of his residents' association and volunteers with Safe City Mississauga as a team leader. Corey said he lives in Ward 6 but has grandchildren, family, friends and neighbours' kids attending schools across various Mississauga wards.

items.title: Caledon OPP seizes drugs, more than $40K following dark web trafficking investigation
items.summary: Police drug trafficking investigation results in numerous charges against two individuals, including a Mississauga resident. An investigation into drug trafficking on the dark web has resulted in numerous charges and the seizure of cash and narcotics, according to the Ontario Provincial Police (OPP). In a news release, the OPP said officers with the Caledon detachment’s Community Street Crime Unit (CSCU) seized more than $40,000 in Canadian currency along with suspected fentanyl and cocaine. Police said an intelligence-led probe began this summer, when the CSCU and OPP Covert Internet Intelligence Unit targeted a dark web operation believed to be shipping high volumes of narcotics. According to the release, police arrested a suspect on Aug. 25 at a Canada Post location in Mississauga, where they seized two packages containing various drugs ready to be shipped across the country. The release said Caledon OPP also executed search warrants at several Greater Toronto Area homes and vehicles with assistance from regional crime units in Dufferin, Kawartha Lakes, Northumberland, Orillia and Peterborough. According to police, items seized during the operation included about 600 grams of suspected fentanyl, about 35 grams of suspected cocaine, drug trafficking paraphernalia and numerous electronic devices. Police said a 33-year-old Mississauga resident faces several charges, including nine counts of trafficking opioids, one count of trafficking cocaine, two counts of possession of opioids for the purpose of trafficking, one count of possession of crime proceeds over $5,000 and 16 counts of failing to comply with a release order.

items.title: City Reverses Course on Aquitaine Avenue Bike Lanes to Restore Fourth Traffic Lane
items.summary: Insauga.com reports the City of Mississauga has removed bicycle lanes from a stretch of Aquitaine Avenue in Meadowvale as part of a plan to restore a fourth lane of vehicle traffic. According to the outlet, a city spokesperson confirmed the bike lanes, introduced in 2023 as part of a pilot project, have been eliminated, with a new in-boulevard multi-use path planned for cyclists and pedestrians instead. The outlet says the original Aquitaine Avenue Road Safety Pilot Project cut the busy four-lane road down to three lanes in summer 2023 to improve safety and reduce speeding, drawing mixed reviews from residents who objected to losing a traffic lane. Insauga.com reports the city decided to undo the pilot and restore the fourth lane following community feedback and new provincial legislation on bike lanes that took effect last December. The change is one of several road-safety initiatives the city has introduced in recent years, according to the outlet.

items.title: Record 44,000-Plus Ballots Cast in Mississauga's Advance Voting, Up 57 Per Cent From 2022
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, 44,049 residents cast ballots during advance voting for the 2026 municipal election. The city reports the advance polls ran from Oct. 6 to 11 at voting locations across Mississauga. City officials say that turnout marks a 57 per cent increase over the 2022 municipal election, when 28,052 ballots were cast in advance. The comparison, the city notes, sets a new high for advance-voting participation in Mississauga. Residents who have not yet voted can do so on Election Day, Oct. 26, at any voting location within their own ward, according to the city.

items.title: City Seeks Volunteers to Keep Mississauga's Neighbourhood Ice Rinks Running This Winter
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, residents can volunteer to help create and maintain natural ice rinks in neighbourhood parks this winter. The city says these rinks give residents free places to skate, play hockey and spend time outdoors through the cold months. Unlike larger skating facilities, the city notes natural ice rinks depend entirely on local volunteers to maintain the ice throughout the season. City officials say 102 volunteers helped run neighbourhood rinks during the 2025-2026 winter season. Residents interested in volunteering can apply online by Nov. 15, according to the city.

items.title: Hospitality Professional Sabir Masih Challenges Incumbent for Mississauga Ward 5 Catholic Trustee Seat
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports three candidates, including one incumbent and two challengers, are running for the Ward 5 trustee seat on the Dufferin-Peel Catholic District School Board. According to the outlet, Metroland sent a questionnaire to every name on the ballot to help voters compare the field. Candidate Sabir Masih told Metroland he works in hospitality and brings experience in education, leadership and community service. Masih said he has not previously held elected office, but has been actively engaged in community development and volunteer work. He said those experiences strengthened his commitment to public service, collaboration, accountability and listening to community needs.
